newsitem.title: USA: Georgia church destroyed in suspicious fire.
newsitem.headline: Georgia church destroyed in suspicious fire.

text.p: Arson may have caused the weekend fire that destroyed a predominantly black, century-old church in central Georgia, authorities said Sunday.

The Oak Grove CME Church in the community of Elko burned before dawn Saturday morning. The church, made of wood and brick and located in a cotton field about 100 miles (160 km) south of Atlanta, had about 40 members.
"We are treating it as a suspicious fire at this point. No determination has been made as to the cause," said Gina Gassert, a spokeswoman for state insurance and fire commissioner John Oxendine.

Gassert said agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco & Firearms, the FBI, the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and local fire officials have gathered evidence from the charred sanctuary and its surroundings.
The fire began about 4:20 a.m. Saturday and the building was engulfed by the time firefighters arrived. An accelerant-sniffing dog was used to comb the burned remains of the church, Gassert said.

Authorities said they had not determined if the fire was caused by arson. Because thunderstorms passed through the area a few hours before the fire was reported, a lightning strike may have been a factor.
A leaky propane tank caused a fire that destroyed a predominantly black church in Laurens County, Ga., earlier this year.
